comments.author: @ericheichstetterpotluck
comments.text:
One thing you don't really appreciate until you're there is how much control goes into those grills. Bittor built them himself, adjusts the height over the coals with a wheel, and even changes the wood depending on the ingredient. He was actually a lumberjack before he became a chef, which feels oddly fitting.

I live in the Basque Country, and it took me a while to realize the fire isn't there to add smoke. It's there to bring each ingredient right to its limit—and no further. Somehow the pea broth, the red prawn, and the chuletón all come off the same grill, yet each one still tastes entirely of itself.
